findings.title: Null/empty destinationCalendar crashes Google Meet fallback
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when destinationCalendar is null or an empty array. The next line then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without optional chaining. This throws a TypeError for any Google Meet booking where the organizer has no destination calendar. handleNewBooking can pass `null`, and many handlers now pass `[]`. Previously `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` was safe. It should be `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Pushing team calendars mutates the event type's destinationCalendar
findings.body: When the event type has a destinationCalendar, evt.destinationCalendar is built as `[eventType.destinationCalendar]`. That fresh array is then mutated with `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)`. Separately, `destinationCalendar` is `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one, so `?.push` silently does nothing and the collective hosts' calendars are dropped. This is the exact multi-host scenario the PR targets. The team members' calendars should be collected into the array unconditionally.

findings.title: Event-type destinationCalendar takes precedence, losing organizer calendar for collective events
findings.body: For collective events, the organizer's own destination calendar is only included when the event type has none. If the event type has one, the host calendars are appended after it. If it has none and the organizer has none, the array is null. The organizer's calendar is therefore inconsistently included. Since teamDestinationCalendars is built from `users.slice(1)`, the first (organizer) user's personal calendar may never get the event.

findings.title: loadUsers rewrite drops organization select and throws for dynamic groups
findings.body: The dynamic-user branch no longer selects `organization: { select: { slug } }`, which the old query included, so downstream code that reads `user.organization` will break or lose data. It also throws if dynamicUserList is empty, and the catch converts every non-HTTP error into a generic 500 'Unable to load users'. This is an unrelated behavioral rewrite inside a calendar fix, with a regression risk for dynamic group bookings.

findings.title: Inconsistent e2e expectations for destinationCalendar
findings.body: Only the BOOKING_REJECTED test was changed to expect `[]`. BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED still expect `destinationCalendar: null`. The confirm handler now yields `[]`, while handleNewBooking can yield null. The payload shape is now inconsistent across events, and there are no unit tests for multi-host behavior.

findings.title: No-op destinationCalendar lookup in updateEvent and deleteEvent
findings.body: `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only reached when externalCalendarId is falsy. The find predicate then compares against a falsy value, so it can never match a real calendar and always returns undefined. The old fallback to destinationCalendar.externalId is silently lost. Update therefore passes an undefined calendarId, and delete falls back to 'primary'. The fallback should use the first destination calendar, or match by credential.

findings.title: Patch after insert uses selectedCalendar without the 'primary' fallback
findings.body: The insert uses `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, but the follow-up `calendar.events.patch` uses `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, which can now be undefined. This happens when no destination calendar matches the credentialId (previously it defaulted to 'primary'). The hangout-link description patch then fails or targets the wrong calendar.

findings.title: Missing credentialId/externalId on fallback event creation; duplicate events possible
findings.body: The `else` branch creates events via `createEvent(c, event)` without passing `destination.externalId`, so the resulting reference gets no externalCalendarId. Reference creation previously used evt.destinationCalendar's values. The loop over every destination calendar plus the 'other_calendar' pass can also create multiple events for the same credential. Each host's destination calendar with the same credential is handled separately, but Google's createEvent picks the calendar by credentialId only, so two destinations sharing a credential produce duplicate events in one calendar.

findings.title: updateEvent called with undefined credential when lookup fails
findings.body: If reference.credentialId is set but neither this.calendarCredentials nor the DB lookup (which also requires `app.slug`) yields a credential, `credential` stays undefined. `updateEvent(credential, ...)` is still called and will throw on `credential.appName`, aborting all remaining references via the catch. The result is that every reference is reported as failed. Skip the reference or push a failure result instead.

findings.title: Recurring cancellation now repeats the delete for every calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring-event branch deletes events for all updatedBookings across all calendar credentials. Previously it ran once because only the first calendar reference was handled. Now it sits inside `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)`. With N calendar references it runs N times, which makes redundant delete calls that return 404/410 and pushes the already-resolved results into apiDeletes.

findings.title: User-facing note string changed unrelatedly
findings.body: 'Notes have been hidden by the organiser' was changed to 'organizer'. Any tests or snapshots matching the old text will break. The change is unrelated to the PR.

findings.title: Inverted slug logic in organization creation changes behavior
findings.body: The original code set `slug` when `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED` and `requestedSlug` when billing is enabled. The new code sets `slug` only when billing IS enabled, which reverses the semantics. This is unrelated to the PR's stated purpose. With billing enabled, orgs are now created with a live slug before payment or verification. With billing disabled, no slug is set at all.
